SG Hawker Hub

A web platform for Singapore hawker centres, where customers order from stalls, vendors run their stalls and NEA officers carry out inspections. I owned four feature areas, from database tables through to the screens.

My role
Developer for queueing, notifications, hygiene grading and eco-friendly packaging
Team
4 students
When
June to August 2026
Built with
Node.js, Express, Microsoft SQL Server, HTML, CSS, JavaScript
Worked with
GitHub branches and merges, Jira, Scrum
Code
Team repository

What I built

  • Digital queue

    Customers, including guests, join a stall's queue and can wander off. Vendors call the next number, pause the queue or close it.

  • Notifications

    Customers hear about queue changes. Vendors get alerts for new orders and complaints, with an unread count on their dashboard.

  • Inspections and hygiene grades

    A separate NEA service with its own officer login. Officers schedule visits and log results, and customers see each stall's current grade.

  • Eco-friendly packaging

    Vendors set their options and surcharges. At checkout, the server re-checks each option in case the vendor changed it after the cart loaded.

These features account for 36 of the platform's 81 API routes.

How a queue alert works

Alerting people at every position change would be noise, so a customer only hears from the system when it matters.

  1. A customer joins and gets a queue number.
  2. The vendor presses Call Next Customer.
  3. The customer being called gets a notification.
  4. Whoever is now three places from the front gets told to come back.

“You are 3 places away. Please make your way back to the stall.”

From inspection to public grade

  1. An officer schedules a visit. A database rule blocks a second visit to that stall on the same date.
  2. The officer logs a score from 0 to 100 with remarks. Officers can only log their own inspections.
  3. The server issues the grade straight away, with an expiry date, so the same score always earns the same grade.
  4. The customer site reads the current grade through a public endpoint. Vendors see their full history.
function suggestGradeForScore(score) {
  if (score >= 90) return "A";
  if (score >= 75) return "B";
  if (score >= 60) return "C";
  return "D";
}

What went wrong, and what I changed

My app couldn't connect to SQL Server until about four days before the deadline, so I had written most of my routes without being able to run them. I had assumed the bug was in my code. One teammate helped me see it was the database connection, and another walked me through the fix. I then spent the remaining days testing and debugging the core flows.

I now check the whole environment, database included, at the very start of a project, and I ask for help much sooner. I also used Claude to help me read error messages and trace a failing login, then corrected the problem myself. That AI use was declared in my submission.

Changi Reunite

A software requirements and design document for a lost-and-found platform across Changi Airport's terminals, replacing paper logbooks and email in the module's brief. I designed how cleaning crew log the items they find.

My role
Analyst and designer for cleaning crew and found item entry
Team
5 students
When
June to August 2026
Built with
UML, Visual Paradigm
Context
Polytechnic module project, not commissioned by Changi Airport Group

My section of the specification

  • Requirements: 5 functional and 5 non-functional, covering login, item logging, photo evidence and shift handover.
  • Use cases: crew login, log found item record and log shift handover to an officer, with a full specification for logging an item.
  • Classes: CleaningCrewMember, FoundItemRecord, ItemCategory and ShiftHandover.
  • Interaction: the sequence diagram below, including its validation and error paths.

Designing for the person holding the phone

Cleaning crew log items on handheld devices during their rounds, so the form has to be built for mobile and confirm a submission within 3 seconds. Category, description and location are mandatory. Up to 3 JPG or PNG photos, 5MB each, record the item's condition as part of the chain of custody.

Keeping five authors consistent

The document went through 7 versions, including changes from lecturer feedback. The final pass lined up the shared class diagram with all five sequence diagrams, adding missing parameters and operations. Any fix touching a teammate's section went to them to confirm first.

Anywheel for smartwatch

How would you find, unlock and return a shared bike from your wrist? I sketched the flow by hand, then redrew it to cover the moments the first version skipped.

My role
UX consultant in a course exercise, working with a classmate as the client
When
October 2026
Method
Rapid paper prototyping
Context
Concept only, not affiliated with Anywheel

What changed in version 2

  • A way out when unlocking fails: the watch explains the tag couldn't be read and offers Try Again or Report Issue.
  • Clear confirmation: a tick and a haptic buzz show the bike is unlocked, then the ride page opens by itself.
  • No accidental endings: ending a ride now asks for confirmation and checks the bike is in a valid parking zone.
  • A proper finish: a summary shows duration, cost, distance and reward points.
  • Less on a tiny screen: the search bar made way for a simple map, the number of bikes nearby and the distance to the closest one.

Gruberoo food delivery

A console food delivery system in C#, modelling restaurants, menus, customers and orders with object-oriented programming.

My role
Developer, splitting features evenly with my partner
Team
2 students
When
January to February 2026
Built with
C#, .NET, Visual Studio, Git, GitHub

The features I wrote

  • Loading data: reading customers and orders from CSV files into linked objects.
  • Listing: showing every restaurant with its menu items.
  • Create order: the longest flow in the program, with input validation at each step so a bad entry prompts again instead of crashing.
  • Modify order: finding a customer's order by email and changing it.
  • Earnings report: for each restaurant, delivered order totals excluding delivery fees and refunds, followed by the overall final amount.

The model uses seven classes: Customer, Order, OrderedFoodItem, Restaurant, Menu, FoodItem and SpecialOffer. Refunded orders are held in a stack, which my report reads from.

Stynoox sales dashboard

An Excel dashboard for the sales manager of a fictional Singapore fashion retailer, built from six years of sales records.

My role
Analyst for the sales manager, one stakeholder per team member
When
June to August 2025
Built with
Excel, Power Query, PivotTables, PivotCharts, slicers
Data
11,266 sales rows from 2020 to 2025, fictional and supplied by the module

I combined two sales sheets into one table and brought in product details with Power Query. The dashboard then answers a sales manager's main questions: sales per year, items sold per store and per brand, sales per brand, and the top sales advisor each year. Slicers filter it by year and item category.

Earlier and shorter work that shows how the rest of my skills developed.

Hawker centre database

Team of 4, January to February 2026. Microsoft SQL Server.

We took a hawker centre brief from an ER model, through mapped relations, to a working database of 18 tables and 19 foreign keys. Rules such as valid grades and expiry dates are enforced by the database itself.

CREATE TABLE Inspection
(
  InspectionID   INT            NOT NULL,
  InspectionDate SMALLDATETIME  NOT NULL,
  HygieneGrade   CHAR(1)        NOT NULL
    CHECK (HygieneGrade IN ('A','B','C','D')),
  GradeExpiry    SMALLDATETIME  NOT NULL,
  OfficerID      INT            NOT NULL,
  StallID        INT            NOT NULL,
  ...
  CONSTRAINT CHK_GradeExpiry
    CHECK (GradeExpiry >= InspectionDate)
);
